newsitem.title: USA: Yeltsin surgery success, Russian PM tells Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin surgery success, Russian PM tells Clinton.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Victor Chernomyrdin telephoned President Bill Clinton on Tuesday and told him President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery had been succesful, U.S. officials said.

Chernomyrdin telephoned Clinton here on U.S. election day to report on the success of the operation, performed earlier Tuesday, a White House official travelling with Clinton said, adding that the conversation was brief.
The official said White House spokesman Mike McCurry would provide further details of the telephone conversation at a briefing expected at about 3.30 p.m. EST (2030 GMT).

In Washington, Defence Department spokesman Ken Bacon also confirmed the conversation with Chernomyrdin, who assumed temporary power as Yeltsin underwent surgery, and said the United States was not concerned about the security of Russia's nuclear weapons stockpile while the operation was under way.
Bacon said: "We believe that adequate steps were taken to oversee and command the nuclear arsenal by turning over government authority to Prime Minister Chernomyrdin."
He noted that U.S. Army Gen. John Shalikashvili, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, made a one-day visit to Moscow on Tuesday for previously-scheduled talks with his Russian counterpart.
